candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XXIV.67. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death'. Ephrem reads the marriage as the comfort-in-grief pattern: legitimate human relationships are God's gift FOR consolation. The narrative pattern (find-bride → marry → be-comforted) is preserved in Tewahedo marital theology as the SAFEGUARD against monastic over-spiritualisation: not everyone is called to monastic celibacy; marriage too is sanctifying.
